subject: Request: launch safeguard commercial accommodation for mux delay
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@fjordanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom@fjordanalytics.com>, procurement@fjordanalytics.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: integration timeline - model-mux rollout

Hi Evelyn,

Quick update from our side: our engineering team ran into an unexpected blocker with the model-mux integration (third-party dependency) that pushes our public launch by ~3–4 weeks. This means the production traffic we planned to route to Redwood will be delayed and our committed pilot usage will be lower for March.

We understand these things happen, but given we already signed an execution plan and budget, Procurement is asking whether Redwood can provide a temporary commercial accommodation (one-time rate offset or credit) to smooth the launch economics while we get back on track.

Can you let us know what options are available and any info you need from us to scope this? Attaching a short usage snapshot that shows expected versus committed consumption for March.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform
Fjord Analytics

-- attachment: usage_snapshot_feb_week2.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@fjordanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom@fjordanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: integration timeline - model-mux rollout

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the heads up and the snapshot. Sorry to hear about the blocker.

We can absolutely discuss a short-term accommodation to bridge the launch gap. To move quickly, can you confirm: 1) the expected % drop vs committed spend for March, 2) whether the launch delay is firm vs a soft estimate, and 3) any contractual constraints from your procurement team (e.g., approval window for credits).

I'll loop in our commercial lead to coordinate options and get an internal approval path started. If you can reply with those 3 items by EOD Friday it would help speed things up.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal - Fjord launch accommodation request

Thanks for flagging, Evelyn. Read the snapshot — Fjord's expected consumption for March looks like a ~62% drop vs contracted pilot spend (their numbers). On product: the mux blocker is tracked in MUX-782 and looks like a dependency on our external model-routing library; engineering estimates 2–4 weeks to resolve if we prioritize.

Commercial recommendation: offer a timeboxed accommodation that preserves Fjord's committed price tier for the original plan but only for the months impacted by the delay (i.e., prorated credit or invoice offset). Two options to propose to the customer quickly:
- Option A (provisional): one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of projected shortfall for March (fast approval, lower cost to us)
- Option B (stronger): guarantee original committed rate for the next two billing periods and provide a reconciliation credit if usage remains below commitment (requires exec sign-off due to dollars/precedent)

If we go with Option B, I recommend we prepare an exec memo outlining precedent risk and financial impact (approx $32k gross over two months per our revenue model). I can draft the memo if you want.

Product ask: can we expedite MUX-782 to a prioritized lane? If engineering can shave even one week off the timeline it materially reduces the accommodation cost.

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 10:03 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — really appreciate the heads up and the snapshot...

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal - Fjord launch accommodation request

Looping back with a draft commercial note attached. I modeled Option B (preserve committed rate for two billing cycles + reconciliation) and included a conditional clause: accommodation is contingent on Fjord resuming normal integration efforts within 45 days.

I've attached the draft (commercial_accommodation_draft.pdf) and included a short exec summary below:
- Estimated gross impact: ~$32,000 across two months (worst case)
- Customer value: preserves launch economics and reduces churn risk for strategic pilot
- Risks: sets a precedent for other pilots if we don't gate approvals and attach timebox/restart conditions

Next step: Evelyn, can you and Karthik sign off to escalate for Marcus/Finance? If yes I'll queue for legal review and prepare a DocuSign proposal.

Monica Patel
Commercial Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

-- attachment: commercial_accommodation_draft.pdf (PDF, 38KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@fjordanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom@fjordanalytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: integration timeline - model-mux rollout

Hi Sarah — thanks for the additional context and patience. We've reviewed internally and prepared a provisional commercial accommodation consistent with our conversation: preserve your committed rate for two billing cycles with a reconciliation credit if usage remains below the commitment. The accommodation is timeboxed and contingent on Fjord resuming integration efforts within 45 days.

We're elevating this to our finance execs for final sign-off (internal note routed to Marcus and Finance). Attached is the draft our commercial team prepared. We'll return with a signed DocuSign offer within 48 hours once we have exec approval.

In the meantime, could you confirm that procurement can accept an accommodation letter (instead of a redline to the Master Services Agreement) so we can move faster? Also, if you can provide the confirmation on expected % drop and whether the delay is firm, we can include that in the final reconciliation language.

Appreciate the partnership — we're keen to keep Fjord's launch on track.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
